professionalSummary.text: Five ranking models released to production search service under traffic ramp from 1% to full traffic, each with release ticket in name
professionalSummary.witness: Released five ranking models to the production search service of the marketplace between 2023 and 2025, each under a traffic ramp from one per cent to full traffic and each on a release ticket in my name.

professionalSummary.text: Handled feature store outage incident in autumn 2024 with incident record in search incident log
professionalSummary.witness: Took on-call duty for ranking incidents throughout that period; the feature store outage of autumn 2024 was mine to handle, and the search incident log carries my incident record for it.

professionalSummary.text: Reviewed live relevance and conversion dashboards after each release and rolled back one release in 2024 due to regression on low-traffic categories
professionalSummary.witness: Read the live relevance and conversion dashboards after every release and in the weekly ranking review, and rolled one release back in 2024 when the conversion dashboard showed a regression on low-traffic categories.

professionalSummary.text: Evaluated models offline against held-out interaction data under agreed protocol with data science before release review
professionalSummary.witness: Evaluated every model offline against held-out interaction data under the evaluation protocol agreed with data science before it went to the release review with the search platform team, where the release ticket recorded which checks were mine.

professionalSummary.text: Wrote model cards for all five models including training window, offline/post-release results, known weaknesses, and hand-over conditions
professionalSummary.witness: Wrote the model card for each of the five models: training window, offline and post-release results, the known weakness on low-traffic categories, and what the next engineer needed to know.

experienceHighlights.text: Coordinated release reviews with search platform team, documenting ownership of checks in release tickets
experienceHighlights.witness: Evaluated every model offline against held-out interaction data under the evaluation protocol agreed with data science before it went to the release review with the search platform team, where the release ticket recorded which checks were mine.

experienceHighlights.text: Maintained weekly ranking review deck tracking dashboard metrics and release outcomes
experienceHighlights.witness: Read the live relevance and conversion dashboards after every release and in the weekly ranking review, and rolled one release back in 2024 when the conversion dashboard showed a regression on low-traffic categories.

projectsAndWorkSamples.text: Five release tickets with traffic ramp records, search incident log for feature store outage, and weekly ranking review deck
projectsAndWorkSamples.witness: Work sample: the five release tickets with their traffic ramp records, the search incident log record for the feature store outage and the weekly ranking review deck for the last quarter.

skills.witness: Released five ranking models to the production search service of the marketplace between 2023 and 2025, each under a traffic ramp from one per cent to full traffic and each on a release ticket in my name.
Took on-call duty for ranking incidents throughout that period; the feature store outage of autumn 2024 was mine to handle, and the search incident log carries my incident record for it.

Read the live relevance and conversion dashboards after every release and in the weekly ranking review, and rolled one release back in 2024 when the conversion dashboard showed a regression on low-traffic categories.

Evaluated every model offline against held-out interaction data under the evaluation protocol agreed with data science before it went to the release review with the search platform team, where the release ticket recorded which checks were mine.
Wrote the model card for each of the five models: training window, offline and post-release results, the known weakness on low-traffic categories, and what the next engineer needed to know.
